subject.title: Feature Request: Masked Secrets - Prevent Agent from Accessing Raw API Keys

question: Should OpenClaw guarantee that selected agent-executed capabilities can use credentials without an agent controlling the normal tool process being able to recover the raw values, and which trusted process or service owns that guarantee?
rationale: Current SecretRefs and hooks reduce exposure but do not define the stronger isolation promise requested here; choosing the trusted dispatch process, supported capability scope, plugin contract, configuration shape, and documented limitations requires secops product intent.

options.title: Core broker boundary
options.body: Define a narrow core credential-broker contract with capability-scoped dispatch-time injection, pluggable vault providers, and end-to-end result redaction.

options.title: Plugin mitigation only
options.body: Keep current generic hooks and document credential-vault plugins as best-effort mitigations without promising agent-blind credentials.

options.title: OS isolation contract
options.body: State that strong separation requires a separate user, sandbox, or proxy and provide supported deployment guidance rather than an in-process masking feature.

recommendation.title: Core broker boundary
recommendation.body: Define a narrow core credential-broker contract with capability-scoped dispatch-time injection, pluggable vault providers, and end-to-end result redaction.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and repeatedly expanded the current external-secret and SecretRef architecture, making them the strongest individual history match for shaping the next contract with secops review.
